classification.difficultyReason: Convert the side ratio into BN=3BC/4, combine it with the midpoint vector, then construct MD and recognise MD=2MN to prove collinearity.

content.prompt:
ABC is a triangle. $\overrightarrow{AB}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=2\underset{\sim}{b}$.

M is the midpoint of AB.

N is the point on BC such that $BN:NC=3:1$.

D is the point such that $\overrightarrow{CD}=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{AC}$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with AC extended to D, midpoint M on AB and N three quarters of the way from B to C. No line MND is supplied.
spec.mathematics: AM=MB; BN:NC=3:1; vector CD is half vector AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; the collinearity line is not drawn.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the vector $\overrightarrow{MN}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use vectors to prove that M, N and D lie on the same straight line.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{MD}=2\overrightarrow{MN}$. These vectors are parallel and share M, so M, N and D are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\tfrac14\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac32\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\tfrac14(\underset{\sim}{a}-6\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=\overrightarrow{MA}+\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CD}\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=-\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+2\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{b}\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=-\tfrac12(\underset{\sim}{a}-6\underset{\sim}{b})\\\overrightarrow{MD}&=2\overrightarrow{MN}\end{aligned}$$
The vectors $\overrightarrow{MN}$ and $\overrightarrow{MD}$ are parallel and share the common point M. Therefore M, N and D are collinear.
